raw_response:
I'm 63 this year, been farming these 16 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. My wife passed five years ago, and my son works construction in Shijiazhuang, so it's just me now. That means I have to watch every yuan, and I need to hire people when it's busy. My knees aren't good anymore, and I can't carry heavy bags like I used to.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10th, same as every year. I buy improved seed from the supply store in town — costs about 15 yuan per mu, I plant about 15 jin per mu. I hire Old Zhang's tractor for rotary tillage and planting, costs me about 25 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time — that's what I've always done, two bags for every two mu. Then in spring, around Qingming, if the wheat looks yellow I'll topdress with about 35 jin of urea per mu. Last year I used more, about 45 jin of urea, but fertilizer prices went up again and I need to save some money for my blood pressure medicine and the maize season. My neighbor Liu used about the same amount last year and got 800 jin per mu, so I figure it's enough.

Irrigation costs a lot now with the electric pump — about 25 yuan per mu each time. I'll water twice for the wheat: once before winter if the soil is dry, and once at jointing stage in March or April. If May is very dry I might water a third time at grain filling, but that's another 400 yuan for the whole field, so I'll wait and see. Two years ago when it was very dry, I watered three times and still only got 700 jin per mu, so I'm not sure the third time is worth it. For weeds, I spray herbicide once after planting. If I see aphids in spring I'll spray insecticide, but only if they're bad — that stuff is expensive.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 12th. The window is tight, only a few days. I use hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu, costs about 35 yuan. I put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer and about 20 jin of urea per mu at planting time, all at once — that saves me a trip and labor. I don't side-dress anymore, too much work for one old man. For irrigation, summer maize usually gets enough rain in July, but if it's dry like last year I'll water once at the big trumpet stage. I might water twice if August is hot and dry, but I hope not. For maize pests, I spray herbicide once, and if there are corn borers I'll use insecticide. Last year the borers were bad and I lost some yield, so this year I'll watch carefully.

I need to hire a combine for wheat harvest — about 50 yuan per mu — and for maize harvest I hire a machine too. Hired labor costs about 100 yuan per day, so I try to do as much myself as I can, but harvest I can't manage alone. My total spending on seeds, fertilizer, water, pesticide, and hired help will be about 9,500 yuan this year. That's most of my savings, so I can't afford any big mistakes. I'd rather put down a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad yield — losing one crop would hurt more than saving a few hundred yuan. If everything goes normal, I expect about 800 jin per mu for wheat and about 900 jin for maize. Not great, not terrible — enough to live on and have some left over.
